record.original_question: Determine whether sporadic Costas arrays form only a finite set, or whether they instead arise from one or more still-unknown generally applicable construction techniques.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Settle the status of sporadic Costas arrays: are they finitely many? Are there new generally applicable construction techniques that produce them?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix (equivalently, a permutation f of {1,2,…,n}) with the property that all the vectors connecting pairs of its 1-entries are pairwise distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer h with |h| < n and every pair of integers i ≠ j in the appropriate range, f(i+h) − f(i) = f(j+h) − f(j) implies i = j. Two main families of Costas arrays are known to exist for infinitely many orders: the Welch construction and the Golomb (Lempel) construction, both based on primitive roots in finite fields. A Costas array is called "generated" if it can be obtained directly from one of these algebraic constructions (using their standard parameters), and "emergent" if it arises from a generated array via a documented operation such as addition or removal of a corner 1, taking sub-arrays, or related transformations. A Costas array that is neither generated nor emergent is called sporadic. Sporadic Costas arrays are presently known only for finitely many orders n with 6 ≤ n ≤ 27, and exhaustive enumeration becomes computationally infeasible for moderately larger n.

Settle the status of sporadic Costas arrays: prove either that the set of sporadic Costas arrays (over all orders n) is finite, or exhibit one or more general construction techniques (independent of the Welch and Golomb families and their known emergent transformations) that produce infinitely many sporadic Costas arrays.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether sporadic Costas arrays are finite in number, or whether some yet-undiscovered general construction produces them, remains open. The Wikipedia article on Costas arrays and recent surveys still describe the existence question for Costas arrays of all orders, and the structural understanding of sporadic examples, as unresolved; no construction beyond Welch/Golomb families and their emergent variants has been found.
